title: Multidisciplinary Studies, B.A. (University College)
notes: Pattern B, though genuinely unlike every other Pattern-B plan in this repo: this major has NO enumerated course list at all, anywhere, per the bulletin's own text -- 'Courses must be selected in consultation with an adviser' for both the 12-credit Core (one course each in Research methods/projects, Communication skills, Theory/application, Critical analysis) and the 24-credit Additional Courses (12 credits at the 400-level from at least three different subject areas including one 3-credit 400-level capstone, plus a minimum 9 credits from the humanities and social sciences) -- confirmed by reading the live bulletin page's own hidden Requirements-for-the-Major DOM text directly (same technique used for PSYCHBA/BS, ITBW, PSCMBW), which genuinely never names a single course code for the major itself. This is NOT the same as an unenumerated-but-restricted 'Technical Elective from department X' pool seen elsewhere in this repo (which at least names eligible departments) -- it is intentionally, structurally open to any university course, subject only to adviser sign-off, level, and subject-area-diversity rules the bulletin states in prose, not in a picklist. Modeling this with a fabricated department scope or a fake course-code list would misrepresent a genuinely adviser-driven, unenumerated major as if it had a real curriculum the way this repo's other majors do -- so every major-requirement item here (Core and Additional alike) is a generic labeled credit-bearing slot with no `options`/`open_elective`/`match` course-resolution attached, and `departments` is intentionally left empty since no course code is ever picked. Gen Ed (45), B.A. Degree Requirements (24: World Language, B.A. Fields, World Cultures), and Electives (15) are modeled the same way every other University-College B.A. in this repo models them (PSYCHBA-2026.json, and the College-of-Liberal-Arts B.A.s like PHILBA/CASBA/SOCBA for the same World Language/B.A. Fields/World Cultures shape) -- generic slots, since the bulletin itself doesn't enumerate a fixed Gen Ed course list either. Total across this plan's 8 semesters is 121 credits against the bulletin's stated 120-credit minimum (45+24+36+15); the 1-credit rounding gap comes from spreading Gen Ed credits across whole 3-credit slots rather than the bulletin's own fractional per-domain breakdown, the same kind of minor reconciliation gap several other plans in this repo note explicitly rather than force an artificial half-credit slot.
